pass_a_gloss: Long ago we heard the words of Jesus and already for much time we have been discipled to the good news, and all of us built for ourselves a house. But where we built, whether upon the rock having dug and having deepened, or upon the sand apart from a foundation, the present struggle will show. For there has set in a winter carrying downpour and rivers and winds, or, as Luke names it, an overflow, and these things, having broken against the house, either will not have strength to rock it, and through this the house will not fall, as founded upon the rock, the Christ, or will convict the decayed state of the building, falling together through the occasion that has set in. Which may it be far off from our buildings; for great exceedingly is the falling in denial, or, as Luke says, great the breach of the building apart from the foundation. Therefore let us pray, so that we may be made like to a prudent man who built his house upon the rock. For let there come upon such a building the downpour from the spiritual things of evil in the heavenly places, or the rivers of the rulers and authorities hostile to us, or the hard winds from the cosmos-rulers of this darkness, or an overflow of the under-earth spirits, and let them break themselves against our building upon the rock; so that, toward not only the not falling but not even the being rocked at all of the house, the working things may rather suffer by us than do. And let each of you say, striking the opposing things: so I fight with fists as not flaying air.
pass_b_english: Long ago we heard the words of Jesus, and for a long time now we have been disciples of the Gospel, and we have all built ourselves a house. But where we built it, whether we dug and went deep and built “upon the rock” (Luke 6:48), or “upon the sand” (Matthew 7:26) “without a foundation” (Luke 6:49), the present contest will show. For a storm has set in, bringing rain and rivers and winds, or, as Luke calls it, a flood. When these have burst against the house, either they will not be strong enough “to shake it”, and so the house will not fall, since it is founded “upon the rock”, Christ; or they will expose the rottenness of the building, which will collapse under the present occasion. May that be far from our buildings! For very great is the fall in denial, or, as Luke says, great is “the ruin” of the building without the foundation.

So let us pray that we may be likened “to a wise man who built his house upon the rock” (Matthew 7:24). Let the “rain” come against such a building from “the spiritual forces of wickedness in the heavenly places” (Ephesians 6:12), or the “rivers” of the principalities and powers that are hostile to us, or the harsh winds from “the world-rulers of this darkness”, or a flood of the spirits beneath the earth; and let them dash themselves against our building that stands “upon the rock”, so that, with the house not only not falling but not even being shaken at all, the powers at work may suffer at our hands rather than act. And let each of you say, as he strikes his adversaries, “So I box, not as one beating the air” (1 Corinthians 9:26).

choices.choice: 2026-11-11: retranslated in full from Koetschau (GCS 2, ch. 48); the old English was a digest: the published English for this chapter was the parable of the sower (ch. 49 material), with 1 Corinthians 3:9, Psalm 92:13 and 1 Corinthians 2:9; nothing of the house on the rock argument was in its place.
'φκχοδομήσαμεν' read as 'ᾠκοδομήσαμεν'; 'ἐπὶ τὴν En' as 'ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν'; 'ἡχέτω' as 'ἡκέτω' ('let come'); 'uns πονηρίας' as 'τῆς πονηρίας'; 'οὃς οὐκ' as 'ὡς οὐκ'.
'the present occasion' (the persecution now at hand), the building collapsing under it.
